key_insight: A unified discrete differential geometry phase-field model can simulate fracture in highly deformable thin structures while capturing the strong coupling between large geometric deformation and crack evolution.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps predict failure, snap-through, and post-fracture reconfiguration in flexible thin structures, supporting more damage-tolerant designs for applications such as flexible electronics.
method: Phase field is defined directly on a triangulated midsurface to model crack initiation and growth.
Membrane and bending energies are computed from discrete geometric measures in a DDG formulation.
A staggered solver with active-set irreversibility and degradation-deletion enables full crack opening and topology updates.
evidence_signal: The paper reports close agreement with geometrically nonlinear finite element results for 2D fracture and captures experimentally observed crack convergence/coalescence in 3D tearing and island-bridge flexible-electronics examples.
watch_item: The degradation-deletion and topology reconstruction steps may be implementation-sensitive and could affect robustness or accuracy near highly complex crack patterns.
paper_title: Phase-Field Fracture Simulation of Highly Deformable Thin Structures via a Discrete Differential Geometry Framework
